flow.text: Three points with no curves, no chords and no neighbours. With the plane empty, every identifier should sit at the NEAREST position that clears its marker — this is the control case for the displacement ranking.

blocks.title: Three isolated points
blocks.caption: Control case — nothing competes, so nothing should be displaced.

slides.title: Identifiers on the axes and on tick values

flow.text: The vertex sits at the origin, where both axes and the printed tick numbers converge — the case raised at the UI-1 visual review. The rest sit exactly ON tick values along each axis, so an identifier and an axis number want the same space.

blocks.title: Points on the axes
blocks.caption: $V$ at the origin plus four points on tick values — identifiers must clear the axis numbering, not just the axis lines.

blocks.title: Points that lie on the geometry

flow.text: Every point lies ON the parabola, and three chords join them. The nearest legal position must clear the curve it sits on and the chords crossing it, so displacement and clearance are in direct tension here.

blocks.title: Points on a curve, joined by chords
blocks.caption: $y=0.5x^2-2$ with five points on the curve and three chords.

flow.text: Points in all four corners and mid-edge. The preferred outward direction leaves the canvas at every one of them, so the nearest LEGAL position is inward — and auto-fit must still expand the domain rather than let a pill run off the plane.

blocks.title: Points at the domain corners and edges
blocks.caption: Edge case — an on-canvas constraint at every marker.

slides.title: Long identifiers in a tight domain

flow.text: Multi-character identifiers make wide pills, and a wide pill clears far less easily than a single letter. Ranking by displacement must not quietly trade a legal position for a nearer illegal one.

blocks.title: Long identifiers at close spacing
blocks.caption: Six wide identifiers inside a small domain.
